disposition_reason: BfR Communication 033/2022 on long-term Ni intake from the MEAL TDS. Its cocoa occurrence values (cocoa powder 11,050, dark chocolate 2,800, beverage powder 2,150 µg/kg) are the same pools already in fechner2022 and are duplicates. Its new cocoa content is exposure: cocoa powder is the 2nd-ranked food for highly exposed adults and the 1st for highly exposed children, plus a note on Ni speciation in cocoa.

study.material_scope: cocoa powder, semisweet/dark chocolate, beverage powder (cocoa drink powder) pools
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Purchased nationwide in Germany (4 regions); growing origin not reported
study.sampling_unit: pooled composite of 15-20 retail items, one pool per food (not stratified)
study.method: ICP-MS (per MEAL methods; details not given in this communication)
study.lod_loq: Ni LOD 6-30 µg/kg, LOQ 20-100 µg/kg depending on food (Table 1 footnote 4)

exposure_context.item: Cocoa powder consumers, adults/adolescents (NVS II, top 5% most exposed; UB)
Cocoa powder consumers, children 0.5-<6 y (VELS, top 10% most exposed; UB)
exposure_context.note: P95 19.37 exceeds the EFSA TDI of 13 µg/kg bw/day; values are total Ni exposure of cocoa-powder consumers, not Ni from cocoa alone.

exposure_context.item: Main food group "Coffee, cocoa and tea" share of total Ni exposure
Chocolate chip muesli among top-10 foods for highly exposed children in mLB scenario (6.18 µg/kg bw/day)
Ni speciation: Ni in cocoa beans mainly organic Ni-gluconate complex (Ni-citrate traces); cocoa powder mainly water-insoluble Ni2+ (citing Peeters et al. 2017)

regulatory.instrument: EFSA CONTAM 2020 scientific opinion (health-based guidance value, not a maximum level)

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary lists children Table 8 foods in P50 order (soy milk, porridge, cocoa powder...); the source ranks cocoa powder 1st (by contribution among foods with >20 consumers) and marks soy milk, porridge, trail mix, millet, spelt bread, sunflower seeds and cashew nuts as n.d. (fewer than 20 consumers). Values themselves match.
Stored summary treats the report as a distinct occurrence source; its cocoa occurrence values duplicate fechner2022 (same pools).
unresolved: Milk chocolate Ni (0.700/0.825 mg/kg in fechner2022) is not separately reported in this communication; organic pools excluded from its tables.
Purchase window (Dec 2016-May 2019) differs from fechner2022 wording (2017-2019) for the same pools.
